q:
Consider the following statements about advance payment on stores bills:
1. Advance payment of up to 98% of the bill value, made against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is initially accounted for under the Purchase Suspense head.
2. This advance is cleared when the material is received and accepted at destination and the balance payment is linked with the bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: Stores imported on 'F.O.B.' (Free On Board) terms means that the price covers:

options.A: Cost, insurance and freight up to the destination port in India
options.B: The cost of the material and its delivery on board the ship at the port of shipment, freight and insurance beyond that point being borne by the buyer
options.C: Only the ex-factory price at the supplier's works
options.D: The cost of the material plus the customs duty payable in India

q: Where stores are purchased on 'F.O.R. destination' terms, a shortage or damage occurring in transit before delivery at the destination depot is:

options.A: The responsibility of the supplier, the transit risk remaining his until the material is delivered and accepted at destination
options.B: Borne by the Railway from the moment of despatch by the supplier
options.C: Borne personally by the depot storekeeper
options.D: Written off without any claim on anybody

q: The Security Deposit furnished by a supplier under a stores contract is liable to be forfeited when:

options.A: The tender in question is discharged without acceptance
options.B: The supplier seeks an extension of the delivery period on genuine grounds
options.C: The material supplied by him is accepted into stock
options.D: The supplier fails to fulfil the contract or to supply the stores satisfactorily in accordance with its terms

q: The Earnest Money Deposit of the tenderers who remain unsuccessful in a stores tender is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.B: Refunded to them after the tender has been finalised and accepted
options.C: Adjusted compulsorily against all their future tenders
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

q: Low-value stores purchases, within the limits laid down in the delegation of powers, may be accepted:

options.A: Only by a Tender Committee of three members in every case
options.B: By the depot storekeeper at his own discretion, whatever the value
options.C: Directly by the competent stores officer, without reference to a Tender Committee
options.D: Only after obtaining the approval of the Railway Board

q: For stores or equipment which are under manufacture, inspection carried out in stages during the process of manufacture itself is known as:

options.A: Stage inspection
options.B: Surprise inspection
options.C: Post-delivery inspection

q: Under a 'firm price' stores contract:

options.A: The supplier may revise his rates every quarter
options.B: The price variation clause applies automatically
options.C: The rates vary with the market price on the date of supply
options.D: The contracted rates remain firm throughout the currency of the contract and are not subject to price variation

q: A supplier who finds that he cannot complete the supply within the stipulated delivery period should apply for extension of the delivery period:

options.A: Only after the liquidated damages have been levied
options.B: Before the expiry of the stipulated delivery period
options.C: Only at the time of submitting his final bill
options.D: At any time within five years after the expiry of the period

q: HML analysis of inventory classifies items on the basis of:

options.A: Their annual consumption value
options.B: Their criticality in use
options.C: Their unit price — High, Medium and Low
options.D: Their rate of movement from the depot

q: Stores items which are both high in annual consumption value ('A' category) and vital in use (VED) call for:

options.A: The strictest inventory control, with close watch on stock levels and consumption
options.B: The loosest control among all categories of items
options.C: No stock being held at all

q: The 'Just-in-Time' (JIT) approach to inventory management aims at:

options.A: Holding the maximum possible stock in depots
options.B: Stocking every item for a full year's consumption
options.C: Doubling the safety stock of all items
options.D: Arranging supplies to arrive just as they are needed for use, so that the inventory held is kept to the minimum

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, within the annual procurement target from MSEs there is a sub-target for MSEs owned by women entrepreneurs of:
Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the local content claimed by a Class-I or Class-II local supplier is:

options.A: Certified by the depot storekeeper
options.B: Certified by RDSO in all cases
options.C: Self-certified by the supplier himself, subject to verification and audit as prescribed

q: Orders banning or blacklisting a firm for supply of stores to the Railways are:

options.A: Circulated to all zonal railways and are effective across the Railways
options.B: Confined to the single depot which issued them
options.C: Kept secret and not communicated to any office

q: Before being offered for sale by e-auction, scrap arising in depots is sorted and segregated according to its description and nature mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase its weight before sale
options.B: Reduce its book value in the accounts
options.C: Delay its disposal as long as possible
options.D: Obtain better realisation (price) in the auction

q: Delivery of scrap sold through e-auction is taken by the purchaser, who is required to:

options.A: Get the material transported to his premises free of cost by the Railway
options.B: Load and remove the material at his own cost within the stipulated delivery period
options.C: Wait until the next auction is held by the depot
options.D: Take delivery at the premises of the original supplier of the stores

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Survey Committee examines unserviceable stores and recommends their condemnation and disposal.
2. The condemnation and disposal of such stores is sanctioned by the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: Debit balances remaining outstanding under Purchase Suspense for a long time generally indicate that:

options.A: Payments have been made to suppliers but the material has not been received or has not been linked, and the balances require follow-up and clearance
options.B: The depot is holding excess stock of stores
options.C: Scrap is awaiting survey and disposal
options.D: Suppliers' bills have not been paid at all

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The lead time for procurement of imported stores is generally longer than that for indigenous stores.
2. On this account, comparatively higher safety stock and coverage are provided for imported items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The maximum stock level fixed for an item guards against over-stocking and locking up of capital in stores.
2. The minimum stock level of an item is the level above which the stock must never be allowed to rise.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: The AAC (Average Annual Consumption) of a stock item is fixed keeping in view:

options.A: The consumption of the item in the last month only
options.B: The production capacity of the supplier of the item
options.C: The book rate of the item in the Priced Stores Ledger
options.D: The past consumption trend of the item and the anticipated future requirements and programmes

q: In stores procedure, a 'demand' is placed by a consuming department on a stores depot, whereas an 'indent' is placed by:

options.A: The supplier on the Railway for supply of stores
options.B: The depot or purchase office for procurement of stores against the demands received
options.C: The Accounts office on the depot for stock verification
options.D: The purchaser of scrap on the depot for delivery of material

q: Through the integrated material management system (iMMS), before placing a fresh purchase order, a depot or purchase office can:

options.A: Cancel all outstanding purchase orders at one stroke
options.B: Fix the rates at which stores are to be purchased
options.C: Ascertain the stock of the item available in other depots and railways, so that a transfer can be arranged instead of a fresh purchase
options.D: Conduct the e-auction of scrap lots

q: The Stores Budget of a zonal railway is consolidated at the headquarters from:

options.A: The requirements furnished by the stores depots and the consuming departments
options.B: The estimates sent directly by the suppliers of stores
options.C: The Stores Budget of the previous year, without any change
options.D: The assessment made by the stock verifiers during stock verification

q: The programme of periodical stock verification of stores depots is drawn up by:

options.A: The custodian of the depot himself
options.B: The suppliers of the stores held in the depot
options.C: The Stores Tender Committee

q: Stores held in a depot are formally declared as surplus by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper on his own authority
options.B: The competent authority, after review of the stock position and circulation of the items to other depots and railways
options.C: The stock verifier who verifies the item
options.D: The purchaser who offers to buy the items

q: Copies of a purchase order placed on a supplier are sent to the consignee depot and to the Accounts office mainly to enable:

options.A: Advertisement of the order in newspapers
options.B: Evaluation of the tenders received against the order
options.C: Linking of the material received and of the supplier's bill with the purchase order
options.D: Fixation of the AAC of the item ordered

q: Stores or scrap can be taken out of a stores depot only against:

options.A: A gate pass issued on the basis of the issue note or delivery order, as the case may be
options.B: A verbal permission given by any depot official
options.C: A copy of the tender notice for the item
options.D: The bin card maintained at the bin

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 80 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 4 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 50 lakh and its Turnover Ratio is 0.25. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 12.5 lakh
options.B: Rs 1 crore
options.C: Rs 2 crore

q: A Turnover Ratio of 0.25 for the stores of a railway indicates that the stock held in depots is broadly equal to:

options.A: 3 months' issues of stores
options.B: 4 months' issues of stores
options.C: 6 months' issues of stores

q: The annual consumption of an item is 1,800 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 2 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:

options.A: 150 units
options.B: 600 units
options.C: 450 units

q: A depot holds 200 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 20 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 28 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 20 per unit
options.B: Rs 24 per unit
options.C: Rs 28 per unit

q: The AAC of an item is 2,400 units. The stock in hand is 700 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 2 months
options.B: 4 months
options.C: 5 months

q: The average consumption of an item is 50 units per week, the lead time is 8 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 200 units. The re-order level of the item is:

options.A: 600 units
options.B: 400 units
options.C: 250 units

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,200 units and the re-order quantity is 900 units. The minimum consumption is 60 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 2,100 units
options.B: 1,500 units
options.C: 900 units

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 120 units per week, its normal consumption is 100 units per week and the lead time is 5 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:

options.A: 600 units
options.B: 100 units
options.C: 500 units

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 90 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 20 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:

options.A: Rs 9 lakh
options.B: Rs 20 lakh
options.C: Rs 18 lakh

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 30 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 350 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:

Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 2,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 3 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 8,00,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 90 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 70 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:

options.A: Rs 70 lakh
options.B: Rs 90 lakh
options.C: Rs 80 lakh

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 40 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.6 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.5 crore. The closing balance of stores is:

options.A: Rs 50 lakh
options.B: Rs 60 lakh
options.C: Rs 30 lakh

q: Scrap having a book value of Rs 75,000 is sold by e-auction for Rs 60,000. The difference of Rs 15,000 between the book value and the sale value is:

options.A: Recovered from the depot storekeeper in all cases
options.B: Credited to the Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: Ignored, as no adjustment is necessary
options.D: Adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account

q: The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) and the Re-order Level of a stock item together answer, respectively, the questions:

options.A: When to order and how much to order
options.B: How much to order and when to order
options.C: From whom to order and at what price
options.D: At what price to order and how much to order

q: GOLF analysis of inventory classifies stores items according to:

options.A: Their annual consumption value
options.B: Their criticality in use
options.C: Their source of supply — Government, Ordinary, Local or Foreign
options.D: Their rate of movement from stock

q: XYZ analysis of inventory classifies items on the basis of:

options.A: The value of inventory (stock) held of the item
options.B: The annual consumption of the item
options.C: The criticality of the item
options.D: The lead time of the item

q: Which of the following is a component of the cost of ordering stores?

options.A: Rent of the godown in which stores are kept
options.B: Interest on the capital locked up in inventory
options.C: Insurance charges on the stock held
options.D: The cost of inviting tenders, inspection and progressing of purchase orders

q: Under the MSMED Act, payment for supplies received from a micro or small enterprise must be made on or before the agreed date, which in no case exceeds:

options.A: 30 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.B: 45 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.C: 60 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.D: 90 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies

q: If a tenderer withdraws his tender during the period of validity of the tender:

options.A: His earnest money deposit is liable to be forfeited
options.B: No action can be taken against him
options.C: He is entitled to compensation for preparing the tender
options.D: His tender is kept pending till the validity expires

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An acceptance of a tender which is qualified or conditional amounts, in effect, to a counter-offer and does not by itself conclude a contract.
2. A contract is concluded only when the offer of the tenderer is accepted absolutely and without qualification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: The Priced Stores Ledger of a stores depot is maintained by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper
options.B: The Stores Accounts office of the Accounts Department
options.C: The purchase office of the Stores Department

q: In a reverse auction conducted on IREPS for the purchase of stores:

options.A: Bidders compete by quoting successively higher prices
options.B: Only the highest bidder is considered for the award of the contract
options.C: Bidding starts from the highest price received in the tender
options.D: Bidding starts from the lowest price received in the tender and bidders compete by quoting successively lower prices

q: The ABC analysis of stores items is required to be revised:

options.A: Periodically, as the consumption pattern and the prices of items change
options.B: Only once, when it is first introduced
options.C: Once in ten years
options.D: Never, once the categories are fixed

q: Safety (buffer) stock of an item is held primarily to guard against:

options.A: Pilferage of stores from the depot
options.B: Obsolescence of the item
options.C: Variations in the rate of consumption and in the lead time
options.D: Rise in the price of the item

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Insurance spares may remain without any issue for long periods, yet they are not treated as surplus merely on that account, as they are held against breakdown contingencies.
2. Vital (safety) items are given priority in stocking so as to avoid stock-outs which may affect the safety of train operations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: Where a purchaser of scrap sold by e-auction does not lift the material within the delivery period allowed, he is liable to pay, in addition to any other consequences under the sale conditions:

options.A: Demurrage charges to the wagon owner
options.B: Ground rent for the period for which the material remains at the depot
options.C: Earnest money deposit afresh

q: Where a loss of stores is established to be due to the negligence of a railway servant:

options.A: The loss is written off in all cases
options.B: The loss is borne by the stores depot as a depot expense
options.C: The loss is recovered from the purchaser of stores
options.D: The cost of the loss may be recovered from the railway servant responsible

q: 'Non-stock' items of stores are those which:

options.A: Are not ordinarily stocked in stores depots and are purchased against specific demands as and when required
options.B: Are stocked in depots in very large quantities
options.C: Are issued to departments free of cost
options.D: Are kept only in railway workshops

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a supplier whose local content is less than 20 per cent is treated as:

options.A: A Class-I local supplier
options.B: A non-local supplier
options.C: A Class-II local supplier

q: Where it is found that tenderers for stores have formed a cartel and have quoted collusive rates, the tender is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted at the lowest rate offered
options.B: Split equally among the members of the cartel
options.C: Finalised after negotiations with the cartel

q: Specialised stores and equipment which are not manufactured in the country may be procured through:

options.A: Local (spot) purchase by the depot
options.B: A single tender placed by the depot officer
options.C: Global tenders invited internationally
options.D: Purchase against the imprest of the depot

q: The earnest money deposit furnished by the successful tenderer in a stores tender is ordinarily:

options.A: Adjusted towards the security deposit required to be furnished under the contract
options.B: Refunded only after the contract is fully completed
options.C: Forfeited to the Railways on placement of the order
options.D: Treated as part payment of the first bill

q: The liquidated damages stipulated in a stores contract represent:

options.A: A penalty imposed on the supplier for delayed supply
options.B: A genuine pre-estimate of the loss likely to be suffered by the Railway on a breach of the contract
options.C: Interest payable on delayed payment of bills
options.D: The profit element of the supplier

q: In a stores contract, the delivery period stipulated in the purchase order is:

options.A: Only an indicative target for the supplier
options.B: Extendable by the supplier at his own discretion
options.C: Of no legal significance
options.D: Of the essence of the contract

q: As a rule, railway stores held in depots are:

options.A: Not insured commercially, the Government bearing its own risk
options.B: Compulsorily insured with a public sector insurance company
options.C: Insured only when their value exceeds a prescribed limit
options.D: Insured by the depot out of its imprest cash

q: Materials management in the Railways embraces:

options.A: Only the purchase of stores
options.B: Only the custody and storage of stores
options.C: Forecasting, procurement, stocking, inventory control and disposal of stores
options.D: Only the disposal of scrap and surplus stores

q: Stores are said to have become 'obsolete' when:

options.A: They have not been issued for a period of 24 months
options.B: The equipment or design for which they were stocked is superseded, even though the stores themselves are serviceable
options.C: They are damaged while lying in the depot
options.D: Their book rate is revised by the Accounts office

q: In the sale of scrap by e-auction, the taxes and duties leviable on the sale are payable:

options.A: By the Railway out of the bid price realised
options.B: By the stores depot conducting the auction
options.C: Equally by the Railway and the purchaser
options.D: By the purchaser, in addition to the bid price

q: Other things remaining the same, if the inventory carrying cost per unit of an item increases, the Economic Order Quantity of the item will:

options.A: Decrease, as smaller quantities will be ordered at a time
options.B: Increase, as larger quantities will be ordered at a time
options.C: Remain unaffected
options.D: Become equal to the annual consumption

q: 'C' category items of stores, which are numerous but of low value, are controlled loosely in that they are:

options.A: Verified by stock verifiers every month
options.B: Stocked with no buffer stock at all
options.C: Purchased in bulk for longer periods, with simple records and control
options.D: Procured only against a Proprietary Article Certificate

q: Suspension of business dealings with a firm, as distinct from banning of the firm, is:

options.A: A permanent measure taken after a full enquiry
options.B: An interim measure adopted pending completion of an enquiry into the conduct of the firm
options.C: A measure applicable only to foreign firms
options.D: A measure taken only by the Railway Board after banning

q: Officers of the Stores Department of Indian Railways belong to the organised Group 'A' service known as:

options.A: Indian Railway Accounts Service
options.B: Indian Railway Traffic Service
options.C: Indian Railway Personnel Service

q: The book (issue) rate of the same stores item:

options.A: Is uniform within a railway, but may differ from one railway to another
options.B: Is the same on all the railways of Indian Railways
options.C: Is fixed by the Railway Board uniformly for all railways
options.D: Differs from depot to depot within the same railway

q: Specifications prescribed for the procurement of stores are required to be:

options.A: Specific to a particular brand or manufacturer
options.B: Drawn up so as to suit a particular firm
options.C: Generic, functional and broad-based, so as not to restrict competition
options.D: Copied from the specifications of the last purchase invariably

q: For the comparison of offers received in a stores tender, the rates are compared on the basis of:

options.A: The ex-works price quoted by the tenderers only
options.B: The total price payable by the Railway at destination, including freight, taxes and duties
options.C: The price quoted by the tenderer recommended by the executive
options.D: The last accepted rate for the item

q: Scrap arising in railway workshops is disposed of by:

options.A: Sale by the workshop itself through local auction
options.B: Destruction under the orders of the workshop officer
options.C: Return to the suppliers of the original material
options.D: Handing it over to the stores depot, which arranges its disposal through e-auction

q: The AAC of an item is 6,000 units. Coverage for four months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 700 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 500 units. The quantity to be ordered is:

options.A: 2,000 units
options.B: 1,200 units
options.C: 800 units

q: A supplier fails to supply 400 units of stores contracted at Rs 85 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 110 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
A stores depot issues 350 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 64 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
Four wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 3 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,500 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
A purchase order is placed for stores valued at Rs 6,00,000. The security deposit prescribed in the contract at 10 per cent of the order value works out to:
The book rate of an item is Rs 250 per unit and the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 20 per cent per annum of the stock value. The carrying cost per unit per year is:

options.A: Rs 20
options.B: Rs 25
options.C: Rs 50

q: The annual requirement of an item is 4,800 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 400 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 300, the total ordering cost per year is:

options.C: Rs 300

q: The average consumption of an item is 150 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 6 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:

options.A: 150 units
options.B: 600 units
options.C: 750 units

q: A depot holds 800 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 40 to Rs 46 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

During stock verification, 12 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 150 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:

options.A: Rs 150

q: Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the Economic Order Quantity of an item is 600 units. The average cycle stock of the item held is:

options.A: 600 units
options.B: 300 units
options.C: 150 units

q: An item has a safety stock of 150 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 500 units. Under the EOQ system, the maximum inventory of the item will be:

options.A: 150 units
options.B: 350 units
options.C: 500 units

q: The cost of stores drawn from a depot by a consuming department or work is charged to the account of that department/work at the time of:

options.A: Purchase of the stores from the supplier
options.B: Issue of the stores from the depot
options.C: Receipt of the stores in the depot

q: During a month, stores bills amounting to Rs 25 lakh were paid and accounted for under Purchase Suspense, and material worth Rs 22 lakh was received at the depots and linked with the bills during the same month. The net amount added to the debit balance under Purchase Suspense during the month is:

options.A: Rs 3 lakh
options.B: Rs 2 lakh
options.C: Rs 22 lakh

q: Where purchased stores are rejected on inspection at the depot, the inspecting authority communicates the rejection to the supplier through a:

options.A: Rejection Note
options.B: Receipt Note
options.C: Bin Card

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balances in the Priced Stores Ledger are reconciled periodically with the balance under Stores Suspense in the General Books.
2. Differences noticed in such reconciliation are investigated and adjusted, so that the priced accounts and the General Books agree.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2

q: Serviceable material released from a completed work and returned to a stores depot is credited to the account of the work at:

options.A: Its original purchase price
options.B: An assessed (fair) value
options.C: Its scrap value

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.05 crore and the total issues during the year are Rs 7 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
Registration of a firm for supply of stores to the Railways is granted:

options.A: Generally for all stores items, without any assessment
options.B: For specific items or groups of items, after assessing the firm's capacity-cum-capability and financial status
options.C: Only to manufacturers located in the same State as the railway
options.D: Only against a security deposit furnished by the firm

q: The warranty period stipulated in a stores contract ordinarily commences from the date of:

options.A: Placement of the purchase order
options.B: Despatch of the stores by the supplier
options.C: Acceptance of the stores at destination (or commissioning, in the case of equipment)

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.2 crore and the closing balance is Rs 80 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:

options.A: Rs 90 lakh
options.B: Rs 1 crore
options.C: Rs 1.1 crore

q: The 'coverage' of a stock item, expressed in months, is computed as:

options.A: AAC divided by the stock in hand
options.B: Stock in hand divided by dues, multiplied by 12
options.C: (Stock in hand − Dues) divided by AAC, multiplied by 12
options.D: (Stock in hand + Dues) divided by AAC, multiplied by 12
